mechanism_narrative: A rebound in WORKPLACES after the prior trough should lift weekday retail trips with a short lag, because more commuters generate more lunch and after-work spending near commercial areas. If the workplace recovery persists for several weeks, RETAIL_REC should rise over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -25.7 at t-1w to -8.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES stays near or above the current level for four weeks but RETAIL_REC does not rise above its last-4-week mean, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in TRANSIT below its recent baseline suppresses spontaneous shopping trips within one week because fewer riders pass through retail corridors. When transit weakness is large, RETAIL_REC should fall relative to the previous four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -25 for a week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT was -27.3 at t-1w and remained negative at t-0w
failure_condition: If TRANSIT remains below -25 for a week and RETAIL_REC is not lower within the next week, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of stronger GROCERY_PHARM activity and weaker PARKS activity indicates substitution toward essential, local errands rather than discretionary outings. That mix should translate into a slight decline in retail-and-recreation over the next two weeks as leisure shopping demand remains soft.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM reached 18.0 at t-0w while PARKS was -5.0
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM stays elevated while PARKS stays depressed but RETAIL_REC rises over the next two weeks, the interaction claim is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility stays above baseline while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain depressed, households are spending more time close to home and fewer trips flow into shopping districts. Under that containment-like regime, RETAIL_REC should weaken over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed positive in all four weeks
failure_condition: If residential time remains elevated while transit and workplaces stay suppressed, yet RETAIL_REC does not fall below its prior 4-week mean, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in PARKS mobility above zero marks better weather and outdoor activity, which should spill over into discretionary shopping trips within two to four weeks. If park use continues to recover, RETAIL_REC should improve relative to the prior month.
candidate_trigger: PARKS crosses above 0 after being negative the prior week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -8.4 at t-2w to 0.4 at t-1w
failure_condition: If PARKS remains at or above zero for two consecutive weeks and RETAIL_REC still does not rise over the next four weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid recovery in GROCERY_PHARM without a matching rise in WORKPLACES signals errand-based movement rather than broad consumer confidence. That pattern should hold retail-and-recreation down over the next one to two weeks because trips are concentrated in necessities rather than discretionary venues.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above 15 while WORKPLACES remains below -5
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM was 18.0 at t-0w while WORKPLACES was -8.9
failure_condition: If grocery/pharmacy stays above 15 and workplaces stay below -5, but RETAIL_REC rises within two weeks, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden recovery in TRANSIT after a prior collapse should raise retail footfall only with a short delay, because improved access reactivates city-center shopping and dining. The effect is conditional on transit rebounding from a very low level.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by at least 5 points week-on-week from a level below -20
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -27.3 at t-1w to -21.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: If TRANSIT rises by at least 5 points from below -20 and RETAIL_REC does not improve within one week, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL and GROCERY_PHARM both remain elevated, households are substituting toward at-home life and local necessity trips instead of leisure shopping. That mix should keep RETAIL_REC below the prior four-week average over the next four weeks, especially if workplaces do not recover.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed positive while GROCERY_PHARM peaked at 18.0
failure_condition: If residential and grocery/pharmacy stay above baseline while workplaces remain weak, yet RETAIL_REC rises over the next four weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.
